What is National Night Out?

{Taken from the website https://natw.org/ }

The National Night Out program culminates annually on the first Tuesday of August. Note: Texas and a select few areas celebrate the first Tuesday of October.

Neighbors participate across thousands of communities from all 50 states, United States territories, Canadian cities, and military bases worldwide.

National Night Out is a really great way to meet your neighbors, to network and put names to faces. You can use it as a springboard to get more organized along the lines of disaster plans for your neighborhood.... i.e. "Which streets around here flood during a downpour?" "Where would the Red Cross be around here if there was an emergency?"

You can also set out a clipboard and collect names of people that might be interested in starting a neighborhood watch group.

But mostly, it's something that families can go to during the week that is free (it's usually a potluck of grill-out) and depending on the city where you live you might get some things to give away (my city had coloring books for the kids and a few T-shirts for hosting last year!)

What I did last year was a pinata(gotta keep the kids entertained), a charcoal grill, and some 2 liters of pop and ice cream for root beer floats, and some basic Dollar Tree supplies - balloons, tablecloths, etc. and jazzed up a local park. Since I registered with my city they had a police car come by and the kids also got to ring the siren... which is super fun for them!

I made a sample donation flier (It had a description of what National Night Out is, and how they could help by donating things) and dropped it at the local grocery store and they donated a cake and a bunch of grill meats which really helped out nicely!

To get the word out, I just printed out some postcard sized black and white invites (so I could get 4 per page) and I just listed the times and to "Bring a chair and a dish to share" and I had a pretty great turnout!

I also listed the party on nextdoor.com but not that many people have heard about it, so the 45minutes I spent walking out invites was well spent.

What are some other things that you could do during an event like this to help the prepping mindset in your community? I have been thinking about printing out some recommendations for my area (tornado, blizzard, heat stroke...pretty much everything besides a hurricane!) and passing them out to people, but making a trivia game and giving out prizes would be more interactive?

Even something about fireworks safety and then obviously lighting some off!

Questions like, "How much water should you keep in your house?"

"1 gallon per person per day" would be the answer I would give, not something along these lines, "At least 7 months worth!" <--- that might give people a strong impression!

What do you think?

Have you ever had a National Night Out party? What kinds of things do you think would be good? Do you already have a 'group' on your block that you get together with? Do you have any experience with a Neighborhood Watch group?
